LESSON: SCALE DRAWING

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Geometry 4.2 Coordinates and graphs (14 lessons) By the end of the sub- strand, 
Topic 4.3: Scale Drawing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 14

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Scale Drawing, part of Geometry 4.2 Coordinates and graphs (14 lessons) By the end of the sub- strand,  in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8 MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: How do we determine scales in real life? 2. How do we use scale drawing in real life situations?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. measure and represent length of different objects from immediate environment in his/her work book in purposive pairs or groups. Those with manipulation difficulties could use appropriate assistive devices or be assisted by peers or teacher to perform the task. Those with poor motor coordination could use any alternative functional part of the body to handle the materials such as strings/ tape measures with loops/ metre rules with grips. Keep learners such as those with brittle bone disease off rugged terrains and slippery grounds to prevent fractures. Those with conditions such as asthma/ epilepsy should be kept off possible triggers such as dust and cold respectively. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. measure and represent length of different objects from immediate environment in his/her work book in purposive pairs or groups. Those with manipulation difficulties could use appropriate assistive devices or be assisted by peers or teacher to perform the task. Those with poor motor coordination could use any alternative functional part of the body to handle the materials such as strings/ tape measures with loops/ metre rules with grips. Keep learners such as those with brittle bone disease off rugged terrains and slippery grounds to prevent fractures. Those with conditions such as asthma/ epilepsy should be kept off possible triggers such as dust and cold respectively. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Scale Drawing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: as the learner discusses and practices converting scale from one form to another

• Critical thinking and problem solving: as the learner discusses and writes given linear scales in statement form.

• Digital literacy: as the learner uses ICT devices to display the maps and use the zoom functions to demonstrate scale.

49

Values

• Responsibility: as the learner makes scale drawings on different learning materials using appropriate scale.

• Citizenship: as the learner uses maps to demonstrate scale and locate places.
